definition_zh: 拼命地；绝望地；极度地
definition_en: in a way that shows no hope is left, or very much
core_image: 一个人用双手扒住最后一格台阶的边缘，指节发白
scene: 电话那头的人一遍遍重复同一个地址，声音越来越急。She searched desperately for the missing key.
sceneCN: 这里 desperately 指「拼命地」（第 1 个义项：用尽全力、不顾一切地）；句意是她拼命寻找那把丢失的钥匙。

senses.title: With every ounce of effort
senses.definition: with great effort because there seems to be no other hope
senses.definitionCN: 因似乎别无希望而用尽全力
senses.example: She searched desperately for the missing key.
senses.exampleCN: 她拼命寻找那把丢失的钥匙。
senses.why: The adverb turns a whole body into one direction.
senses.whyCN: 这个副词把整个身体拧成一个方向。

senses.title: With all hope gone
senses.definition: in a way that shows every hope has already been lost
senses.definitionCN: 以显示出所有希望都已失去的方式
senses.example: He looked desperately at the closed gate.
senses.exampleCN: 他绝望地看着那扇关上的大门。
senses.why: The same intensity can come from effort or from its failure.
senses.whyCN: 同样的强度，可以来自用力，也可以来自用力的失败。

senses.title: Very much indeed
senses.definition: used in everyday speech to mean very much
senses.definitionCN: 在日常口语中用来表示程度非常深
senses.example: She was desperately tired after the night shift.
senses.exampleCN: 夜班之后她累极了。
senses.why: Intensity borrowed from despair becomes a plain intensifier.
senses.whyCN: 从绝望那里借来的强度，最后成了一个普通的程度词。

intro.en: Desperately is desperate plus -ly, and desperate goes back to Latin desperatus, a person past all hope.
intro.cn: desperately 是 desperate 加 -ly，而 desperate 可追到拉丁语 desperatus，指已越过所有希望的人。

items.en: Desperatus was the past participle of desperare, to lose hope.
items.cn: desperatus 是 desperare（失去希望）的过去分词。

items.en: The root spes, hope, is hidden inside the adverb still.
items.cn: 词根 spes（希望）至今仍藏在这个副词里。

items.en: The adverb appeared beside the adjective in written English.
items.cn: 这个副词在书面英语里与形容词一同出现。

items.en: It began to modify verbs of trying as well as verbs of feeling.
items.cn: 它开始修饰表示尝试的动词，而不只是表示感受的动词。

items.en: In speech it now simply means very, as in desperately tired.
items.cn: 在口语里它如今只表示非常，如累极了。

note.en: The look-alike group all share the hope root, and the meaning group runs from urgency to plain hopelessness.
note.cn: 形近组都共用表示希望的词根，近义组则从急迫一路走到彻底无望。

entries.definition: ready to risk anything
the state of having no hope
the feeling that nothing can be done
in a way that needs action at once
entries.definitionCN: 以需要立刻行动的方式

entries.definition: in a wild and hurried way
in a way that offers no hope

normalIntro.en: These hooks begin with white knuckles on a stone step and end with a voice repeating an address.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从石阶上发白的指节开始，落到反复念着一个地址的声音。

normal.en: Desperately is desperate wearing an adverb's coat.
normal.cn: desperately 就是披着副词外衣的 desperate。

normal.en: The word still carries a hidden hope inside it.
normal.cn: 这个词里还藏着一个「希望」。

normal.en: When the hands pull hardest, the adverb shows up.
normal.cn: 双手最用劲的时候，这个副词就出现了。

normal.en: A tired adverb becomes a simple word for very.
normal.cn: 一个疲累的副词，最后成了「非常」的简单说法。

normal.en: Desperately poor and desperately late share one tone.
normal.cn: 极度贫困与急得迟到，用的是同一种口气。

abstract.en: Picture fingers gripping a ledge until the skin turns pale.
abstract.cn: 想象手指扣住边沿，直到皮肤发白。

abstract.en: Picture a mouth saying the same street name again and again.
abstract.cn: 想象一张嘴一遍遍念同一个街名。

abstract.en: Picture a runner who has stopped looking at the finish line.
abstract.cn: 想象一个已经不再看终点的奔跑者。

examples.en: She searched desperately for the missing key.
examples.cn: 她拼命寻找那把丢失的钥匙。

examples.en: He looked desperately at the closed gate.
examples.cn: 他绝望地看着那扇关上的大门。

examples.en: She was desperately tired after the night shift.
examples.cn: 夜班之后她累极了。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 desperately 记成「地死怕特利」：怕到极点，做事就带上拼命的劲头。

root: 由 desperate 加后缀 -ly 构成，desperate 则来自拉丁语 desperatus，是 desperare（失去希望）的过去分词，词根为 spes（希望）。本义是以希望耗尽的方式做事，后来既指用尽全力，也指心里彻底无望，口语中又弱化为程度副词。

sensesIntro.en: From effort at full strength, to the look of lost hope, to a casual word for very.
sensesIntro.cn: 从全力使出的劲，到失去希望的神色，再到口语里表示非常。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: fingers holding on with the last of their strength.
core.cn: 核心意象：手指用最后一点力气扣住不放。

branches.en: The first sense is strength pushed to its limit.
branches.cn: 第一个义项是力气被推到极限。

branches.en: The second sense is the face after the limit is passed.
branches.cn: 第二个义项是越过极限之后的那张脸。

branches.en: The third sense is the same force worn down into emphasis.
branches.cn: 第三个义项是同一股力道被磨成了强调。

branches.en: Effort and hopelessness are two readings of the same tight grip.
branches.cn: 用力与绝望，是同一只紧握的手的两种读法。

branches.en: A word for survival effort can end up meaning merely very tired.
branches.cn: 一个表示求生力气的词，最后可以只表示累得不行。

intro.en: Desperately belongs to the hope family and adds the ending that turns it into a manner word.
intro.cn: desperately 属于「希望」这一族，加上后缀后成为一个表示方式的词。

latinIntro.en: The base is Latin spes, hope, with de- removing it and -ly marking the adverb in English.
latinIntro.cn: 它的词基是拉丁语 spes（希望），de- 把它移走，英语再用 -ly 标出副词。

items.example: She tried desperately to hold on.

items.meaning: the state of having no hope
items.example: In desperation he sold the car.
items.exampleCN: 走投无路之下他卖掉了车。

items.example: There was a strange desperateness in his voice.
items.exampleCN: 他的声音里有一种奇怪的不顾一切。

items.example: The desperado rode off at dawn.
items.exampleCN: 那个亡命之徒天亮时骑马走了。
她发出一声绝望的叫喊。

definition_zh: 尽管；虽然；不顾
definition_en: used to say that something happens even though another thing could have stopped it
core_image: 雨水顺着伞骨往下淌，伞下的人仍旧往前走
scene: 风把海报吹得翻卷起来，来听讲座的人还是坐满了屋子。Despite the heavy rain, the whole class came on time.
sceneCN: 这里 despite 指「尽管」（第 1 个义项：表示某事没有被另一情况阻止）；句意是尽管下着大雨，全班还是准时到了。

senses.title: It happened anyway
senses.definition: used before a noun to show that something did not prevent an action
senses.definitionCN: 用在名词前，表示某情况并未阻止某个动作
senses.example: Despite the heavy rain, the whole class came on time.
senses.exampleCN: 尽管下着大雨，全班还是准时到了。
senses.why: One force pushes, and the thing still moves the other way.
senses.whyCN: 一股力量推过来，那件事却仍旧朝另一边走。

senses.title: Against someone's wishes
senses.definition: used before a noun to show that an action goes against what someone wants or feels
senses.definitionCN: 用在名词前，表示某行为违背某人的意愿或情感
senses.example: Despite his family's wishes, he left the farm for the city.
senses.exampleCN: 不顾家人的意愿，他离开农场去了城市。
senses.why: The word once meant looking down on someone, and a trace of that refusal remains.
senses.whyCN: 这个词从前指俯视某人，那种不理会至今还留着一丝痕迹。

intro.en: Despite came from Old French despit, contempt, from Latin despectus, a looking down on, built on de- and specere, to look.
intro.cn: despite 来自古法语 despit（轻蔑），源于拉丁语 despectus（俯视），由 de- 与 specere（看）构成。

items.en: Specere meant to look, and despicere meant to look down on.
items.cn: specere 指看，despicere 指往下看、瞧不起。

items.en: Despectus named the contempt itself.
items.cn: despectus 指的就是这种轻蔑本身。

items.en: Despit carried both scorn and the phrase in despite of.
items.cn: despit 既带着蔑视，也带着 in despite of 这个说法。

items.en: English shortened the phrase until despite stood alone as a preposition.
items.cn: 英语把这个短语越缩越短，最后 despite 独自成了介词。

items.en: The scorn faded, leaving only the sense of something not stopping you.
items.cn: 轻蔑的色彩淡去，只留下「某事拦不住你」这一层。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the spit or spect shape, and the meaning group all mark a contrast that did not change the result.
note.cn: 形近组共用 spit 或 spect 的形状，近义组则都标记一种没能改变结果的对照。

entries.definition: a wish to hurt someone
full of a wish to hurt
to feel strong contempt for someone
in spite of a fact
even though something is true
without being affected by something

normalIntro.en: These hooks begin with rain running off an umbrella and end with a family waving goodbye at a gate.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从雨水顺着伞骨往下淌开始，落到门口挥手告别的家人。

normal.en: Despite sets up a wall and then walks straight through it.
normal.cn: despite 先砌一堵墙，然后径直穿过去。

normal.en: The word once meant looking down, so it still refuses to bow.
normal.cn: 这个词从前指往下看，所以至今也不肯低头。

normal.en: Despite takes a noun; although takes a whole sentence.
normal.cn: despite 后面接名词，although 后面接一整句。

normal.en: Rain, warnings, wishes: all can follow despite and change nothing.
normal.cn: 雨、警告、家人的意愿，都能跟在 despite 后面，却什么也改变不了。

normal.en: Despite everything is what people say when they are still standing.
normal.cn: 还站着的人，才会说 despite everything。

abstract.en: Picture an umbrella bent forward against a strong wind.
abstract.cn: 想象一把伞顶着大风向前倾。

abstract.en: Picture wet footprints leading into a dry hall.
abstract.cn: 想象一串湿脚印一直通向干燥的大厅。

abstract.en: Picture a packed room while the storm hits the windows.
abstract.cn: 想象窗外风雨拍打，屋里却坐满了人。

examples.en: Despite the heavy rain, the whole class came on time.
examples.cn: 尽管下着大雨，全班还是准时到了。

examples.en: Despite his family's wishes, he left the farm for the city.
examples.cn: 不顾家人的意愿，他离开农场去了城市。

examples.en: The plan failed despite all their efforts.
examples.cn: 尽管他们尽了全力，计划还是失败了。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 despite 记成「地死拜特」：de 是去掉，spite 是阻碍，阻碍被去掉，事情照做，就是尽管。

root: 来自古法语 despit（轻蔑），源于拉丁语 despectus（俯视），由 de-（向下）与 specere（看）构成。本义是瞧不起、不放在眼里，短语 in despite of 逐渐缩成介词，表示某情况存在却没能阻止某事，也指不顾某人的意愿。

sensesIntro.en: From a look of contempt, to a preposition that lets an obstacle stand and then walks past it.
sensesIntro.cn: 从轻蔑的一瞥，到一个先让障碍站着、再从旁边走过去的介词。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an obstacle standing still while the action passes it.
core.cn: 核心意象：障碍站着不动，行动却从旁边过去了。

branches.en: The first sense is an obstacle that fails to stop anything.
branches.cn: 第一个义项是一个没能拦住任何事的障碍。

branches.en: The second sense is a person's wish treated the same way.
branches.cn: 第二个义项是某人的意愿被同样对待。

branches.en: Rain, cost and distance are the usual things it stands before.
branches.cn: 雨、代价与距离，是它最常挡在前面的东西。

branches.en: A storm and a family's advice both count as things not listened to.
branches.cn: 一场暴雨与家人的劝告，都算作没被听从的东西。

branches.en: The old contempt survives only as this quiet refusal to yield.
branches.cn: 古老的轻蔑只剩下这一点安静的、不肯让步。

intro.en: Despite is tied to a family of looking down and of spite, which still colours the modern preposition.
intro.cn: despite 与一族表示俯视和怨恨的词相连，这层色彩至今还在影响这个介词。

latinIntro.en: The base is Latin specere, to look; de- points the look downward, and despicere means to scorn.
latinIntro.cn: 它的词基是拉丁语 specere（看），de- 把目光转向下方，despicere 就是轻视。

items.example: They went out despite the cold.
items.exampleCN: 尽管很冷，他们还是出门了。

items.example: He said it out of spite.

items.meaning: full of a wish to hurt

items.example: The old rule was widely despised.

items.exampleCN: 他离开时没有鄙视任何人。

definition_zh: v. 掠夺；剥夺；抢夺（尤指以武力夺走财物或毁坏美好之物）
definition_en: to rob a place or person of goods or valuables by force, or to ruin the beauty of something
core_image: 士兵把村民的粮袋搬上马车，屋里只剩空柜；果园的果子被摘光，枝条空着
scene: 入侵者掠夺了村里的粮食。The invaders despoiled the village of its grain.
sceneCN: 第 1 个义项：despoiled 指掠夺、抢走；句意是入侵者掠夺了村里的粮食。

senses.title: Plunder a place
senses.definition: to rob a place of its goods or valuables by force
senses.definitionCN: 用武力抢走一个地方的财物
senses.example: The invaders despoiled the village of its grain.
senses.exampleCN: 入侵者掠夺了村里的粮食。
senses.why: Grain sacks loaded onto a cart outside an empty house.
senses.whyCN: 粮袋被搬上马车，屋子空了。

senses.title: Strip of what is valued
senses.definition: to take away something valuable or cherished from a person or thing
senses.definitionCN: 从人或物身上拿走珍贵或被珍视的东西
senses.example: The quarry despoiled the hillside of its trees.
senses.exampleCN: 采石场夺走了山坡上的树木。
senses.why: A bare slope where an orchard once stood.
senses.whyCN: 曾经果园所在的一片秃坡。

senses.title: Ruin beauty or quality
senses.definition: to spoil the beauty or quality of something
senses.definitionCN: 破坏某物的美感或品质
senses.example: Billboards despoil the view from the bridge.
senses.exampleCN: 广告牌毁掉了桥上的风景。
senses.why: A row of signs blocking a river view.
senses.whyCN: 一排挡住河景的招牌。

intro.en: Despoil comes from Latin despoliare, de- plus spoliare, to strip or plunder, from spolium, skin taken from an animal and then booty.
intro.cn: despoil 源自拉丁语 despoliare，由 de- 加 spoliare（剥去、掠夺）构成，spoliare 来自 spolium（剥下的兽皮，引申为战利品）。

items.en: Spolium meant skin stripped from an animal, then booty.
items.cn: spolium 原指剥下的兽皮，后指战利品。

items.en: Spoliare meant to strip or plunder.
items.cn: spoliare 意为剥去、掠夺。

items.en: Despoliare meant to plunder thoroughly.
items.cn: despoliare 意为彻底掠夺。

items.en: Despoillier carried the sense into French.
items.cn: 古法语 despoillier 承接了这个意思。

items.en: Despoil entered English for robbing a place.
items.cn: 十四世纪 despoil 以劫掠某地义进入英语。

items.en: It now also covers ruining a landscape.
items.cn: 如今它也用于描述毁坏景观。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the spoil- strip family; the near-meaning group names other ways of taking by force.
note.cn: 形近组共享 spoil-（剥去）家族；近义组是其他「强行拿走」的说法。

entries.definition: To damage or ruin something; it shares the spolium root but lost the plunder sense.
entries.definitionCN: 损坏、糟蹋；共享 spolium 词根，但失去了掠夺义。

entries.definition: The act of plundering or ruining, especially in war.
entries.definitionCN: 掠夺或毁坏的行为，尤指战争中。

entries.definition: The amount of food or goods that has gone bad.
entries.definitionCN: 变质损耗的食物或货物量。

entries.definition: To steal goods from a place by force, especially in war.
entries.definitionCN: （尤指战时）武力抢走某地财物。

entries.definition: To steal from shops or houses during a riot or war.
entries.definitionCN: 在骚乱或战争中抢劫商店、住宅。

entries.definition: To damage something severely.

normalIntro.en: Despoil is de- fully plus spoil- strip: strip a place until nothing of value is left.
normalIntro.cn: despoil 就是 de-（彻底）加 spoil-（剥去）：把一个地方剥到不留任何值钱的东西。

normal.en: Spoil- comes from spolium, skin stripped off.
normal.cn: spoil- 来自 spolium，剥下的皮。

normal.en: De- adds the sense of completely.
normal.cn: de- 加上彻底的意思。

normal.en: Despoil takes of, like deprive.
normal.cn: despoil 和 deprive 一样后接 of。

normal.en: Despoil the land means strip it bare.
normal.cn: despoil the land 就是把土地剥光。

normal.en: Spoliation is the noun for the act.
normal.cn: spoliation 是这一行为的名词。

abstract.en: Grain sacks loaded onto a cart outside an empty house.
abstract.cn: 粮袋被搬上马车，屋子空了。

abstract.en: A bare slope where an orchard once stood.
abstract.cn: 曾经果园所在的一片秃坡。

abstract.en: A row of signs blocking a river view.
abstract.cn: 一排挡住河景的招牌。

examples.en: The army despoiled the temple of its statues.
examples.cn: 军队掠走了庙里的雕像。

examples.en: Mining has despoiled the valley.
examples.cn: 采矿毁掉了这条山谷。

examples.en: They despoil the coast with rubbish.
examples.cn: 他们用垃圾糟蹋海岸。

dict_mnemonic.text: despoil ＝ de（彻底）＋ spoil（剥去、掠夺，与 spoil 同源拉丁语 spolium「剥下的兽皮、战利品」）＝把一个地方彻底剥光，「掠夺」。

root: 拉丁语 spolium（剥下的兽皮、战利品）→ spoliare（剥去、掠夺）→ de-＋spoliare → despoliare → 古法语 despoillier → 英语 despoil

sensesIntro.en: One place stripped bare: a village, a hillside and a river view.
sensesIntro.cn: 同一个被剥光的地方：一座村庄、一面山坡与一段河景。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: grain sacks loaded onto a cart while the village cupboard stands empty
core.cn: 核心意象：粮袋被搬上马车，村里的柜子空着

branches.en: Grain sacks loaded onto a cart outside an empty house.
branches.cn: 粮袋被搬上马车，屋子空了。

branches.en: A bare slope where an orchard once stood.
branches.cn: 曾经果园所在的一片秃坡。

branches.en: A row of signs blocking a river view.
branches.cn: 一排挡住河景的招牌。

branches.en: Both strip a place of what it holds.
branches.cn: 两者都把一个地方拥有的东西剥走。

branches.en: Both leave something poorer than before.
branches.cn: 两者都让事物比从前更贫乏。

intro.en: Despoil is de- plus spoil-; the strip root also builds spoil and spoliation.
intro.cn: despoil 由 de- 加 spoil- 构成；剥去这个词根也造出 spoil 与 spoliation。

latinIntro.en: Latin spolium means stripped skin or booty, spoliare to plunder and rapere to seize.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 spolium 意为剥下的皮或战利品，spoliare 意为掠夺，rapere 意为抓取。

definition_zh: 目的地；终点；旅游胜地
definition_en: the place that someone or something is travelling to
core_image: 长途车窗外的路牌，一个地名后面跟着一支箭头
scene: 大巴在夜里开了很久，司机终于报出那个熟悉的地名。After ten hours on the road, they reached their destination.
sceneCN: 这里 destination 指「目的地」（第 1 个义项：旅程要去的地方）；句意是在路上走了十个小时后，他们到达了目的地。

senses.title: The place you are going to
senses.definition: the place that a person or vehicle is travelling toward
senses.definitionCN: 人或车辆正在前往的那个地方
senses.example: After ten hours on the road, they reached their destination.
senses.exampleCN: 在路上走了十个小时后，他们到达了目的地。
senses.why: A journey needs one fixed point for every turn to point at.
senses.whyCN: 一段旅程需要一个固定的点，让每一次转弯都有所指。

senses.title: The end of the line
senses.definition: the final stop on a route or transport service
senses.definitionCN: 某条路线或交通线路的最后一站
senses.example: This train's destination is the coast.
senses.exampleCN: 这趟列车的终点是海边。
senses.why: Tracks end somewhere, and the map must name that end.
senses.whyCN: 轨道总在某处结束，地图必须给那个结束命名。

senses.title: A place people travel to
senses.definition: a place that many people choose to visit for pleasure
senses.definitionCN: 许多人为了游玩而选择前往的地方
senses.example: The old port is now a favourite destination for divers.
senses.exampleCN: 这座旧港口如今是潜水者喜爱的去处。
senses.why: When enough people aim at one place, the place becomes the word.
senses.whyCN: 当足够多的人朝同一个地方去，那个地方就成了这个词本身。

intro.en: Destination comes from Latin destinare, to fix or make firm, built on de- and stare, to stand, so a destination is a point fixed to stand at.
intro.cn: destination 来自拉丁语 destinare（固定、定下），由 de- 与 stare（站立）构成，目的地就是一个被定住要站到的点。

items.en: Stare meant to stand, and destinare meant to make something stand firm.
items.cn: stare 指站立，destinare 指使某物稳稳立住。

items.en: It was used for fixing a purpose, a date or a place in advance.
items.cn: 它用于事先定下目的、日期或地点。

items.en: Destinatio named the act of fixing, and later the fixed point.
items.cn: destinatio 指固定的动作，后来指被固定的那个点。

items.en: French destination carried the travel sense into English.
items.cn: 法语 destination 把旅行的意思带进了英语。

items.en: Tourism turned the word into a label for places worth visiting.
items.cn: 旅游业又把这个词变成值得一去的那些地方的标签。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the destin- stem of fate and fixing, and the meaning group all name an end point.
note.cn: 形近组共用 destin- 这个表示命运与固定的词干，近义组则都指一个终点。

entries.definition: what is fated to happen to someone
entries.definitionCN: 某人命中注定要遇到的事

entries.definition: certain to happen or to go somewhere
entries.definitionCN: 注定发生或注定前往的

entries.definition: to set aside for a purpose
the result you are trying to reach
the last stop of a bus or train line
entries.definitionCN: 公交线或铁路的终点站

entries.definition: an aim that is chosen in advance

normalIntro.en: These hooks begin with a road sign at night and end with a harbour full of divers.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从夜里的一块路牌开始，落到一个挤满潜水者的港口。

normal.en: A destination is a point the map has agreed to stand still for.
normal.cn: 目的地就是地图答应站着不动的那一点。

normal.en: Destinare meant to fix, so the place is fixed before you leave.
normal.cn: destinare 本是固定，所以地方在你出发前就定好了。

normal.en: A train has a destination; a walk may only have a direction.
normal.cn: 列车有目的地，散步有时只有方向。

normal.en: When a place draws crowds, it becomes a destination by itself.
normal.cn: 一个地方招来人群，它自己就成了目的地。

normal.en: The word shares a stem with destiny, which is a destination in time.
normal.cn: 这个词与 destiny 同根，命运不过是时间里的目的地。

abstract.en: Picture a white arrow on a dark blue sign.
abstract.cn: 想象深蓝色路牌上的一支白色箭头。

abstract.en: Picture a bus door opening onto a lit platform at midnight.
abstract.cn: 想象午夜车门打开，外面是一处亮着灯的站台。

abstract.en: Picture a suitcase set down at the end of a long lane.
abstract.cn: 想象一只箱子被放在一条长巷的尽头。

examples.en: After ten hours on the road, they reached their destination.
examples.cn: 在路上走了十个小时后，他们到达了目的地。

examples.en: This train's destination is the coast.
examples.cn: 这趟列车的终点是海边。

examples.en: The old port is now a favourite destination for divers.
examples.cn: 这座旧港口如今是潜水者喜爱的去处。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 destination 记成「地斯提内神」：de 向下，st 像「站」，定住站下的那个点，就是目的地。

root: 来自拉丁语 destinare（固定、定下），由 de- 与 stare（站立）构成，名词 destinatio 指固定的动作与固定的点，经法语进入英语。本义是被定下来要到达的地方，后来指交通线路的终点，也指人们专程前往的旅游地。

sensesIntro.en: From the point a journey aims at, to the end of a line, to a place that draws travellers by itself.
sensesIntro.cn: 从旅程所指向的点，到一条线路的尽头，再到本身就能招来旅人的地方。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a fixed point on a map with an arrow pointing to it.
core.cn: 核心意象：地图上一个被箭头指着的固定点。

branches.en: The first sense is the point a traveller keeps aiming at.
branches.cn: 第一个义项是旅人一直对准的那个点。

branches.en: The second sense is where the rails simply stop.
branches.cn: 第二个义项是铁轨干脆停下的地方。

branches.en: The third sense is a point that attracts many journeys at once.
branches.cn: 第三个义项是同时吸引许多旅程的一个点。

branches.en: A personal aim and a timetable's last stop share the same arrow.
branches.cn: 个人的目标与时刻表的最后一站，共用同一支箭头。

branches.en: Enough private journeys turn a place into a public destination.
branches.cn: 足够多的私人旅程，会把一个地方变成公共的去处。

intro.en: Destination belongs to a family about fixing a point, which also grows the words for fate.
intro.cn: destination 属于一族表示「定下一个点」的词，这一族还长出了表示命运的词。

latinIntro.en: The base is Latin stare, to stand, and de- makes the standing firm and settled.
latinIntro.cn: 它的词基是拉丁语 stare（站立），前缀 de- 让这站立变得稳固、确定。

items.example: We reached our destination at dusk.

这条线路通往五个目的地。

items.example: They destined the land for a park.
items.exampleCN: 他们把那块地定为公园。

items.example: Chance destines some plans to fail.
items.exampleCN: 偶然让一些计划注定失败。

items.example: They were destined to meet again.

items.meaning: the act of fixing a purpose
items.example: Destining the site took a week.
items.exampleCN: 为这块地定用途花了一周。

items.meaning: what is fixed for a person
items.exampleCN: 他平静地接受了自己的命运。
这场战争把他们的命运连在一起。

definition_zh: n. 命运；定数；天命；（重大的）使命
definition_en: the events that will happen to a person, thought of as fixed in advance, or the power believed to decide them
core_image: 一条铁轨在雾里向前延伸，道岔早已扳好；一个人站在路口，脚下的路只有一条
scene: 她相信命运掌握在自己手里。She believed her destiny was in her own hands.
sceneCN: 第 1 个义项：destiny 指命运、注定的走向；句意是她相信命运掌握在自己手里。

senses.title: What is fated to happen
senses.definition: the events that will happen to a person, thought of as fixed in advance
senses.definitionCN: 被认为事先已定好、将发生在一个人身上的事
senses.example: She believed her destiny was in her own hands.
senses.exampleCN: 她相信命运掌握在自己手里。
senses.why: A single rail running forward into fog.

senses.title: A power that fixes events
senses.definition: a power that is believed to decide what will happen
senses.definitionCN: 被认为决定事情走向的力量
senses.example: They took the storm as a sign of destiny.
senses.exampleCN: 他们把这场风暴当作天意的征兆。
senses.why: A switch already set on a track junction.
senses.whyCN: 道岔口一个早已扳好的开关。

senses.title: A great purpose ahead
senses.definition: an important future role that someone seems meant to fulfil
senses.definitionCN: 某人似乎注定要承担的重要未来角色
senses.example: He felt a sense of destiny about the mission.
senses.exampleCN: 他对这项任务怀有一种使命感。
senses.why: A young officer handed a sealed map.
senses.whyCN: 一位年轻军官接过一张密封的地图。

intro.en: Destiny comes from Latin destinare, to make firm or appoint, built on stare, to stand, and reached English through Old French destinee.
intro.cn: destiny 源自拉丁语 destinare（使确定、指定），建立在 stare（站立）之上，经古法语 destinee 进入英语。

items.en: Stare meant to stand.
items.cn: stare 意为站立。

items.en: Destinare meant to make firm or appoint.
items.cn: destinare 意为使确定、指定。

items.en: Destinee meant what has been appointed.
items.cn: 古法语 destinee 意为被指定好的事。

items.en: Destiny entered English for fate.
items.cn: 十四世纪 destiny 以命运义进入英语。

items.en: It also named the power behind events.
items.cn: 十六世纪它也指事件背后的力量。

items.en: A sense of destiny now means a calling.
items.cn: 如今 a sense of destiny 指使命感。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the destin- appoint family; the near-meaning group names other words for what is fated.
note.cn: 形近组共享 destin-（指定）家族；近义组是其他表示「注定」的词。

entries.definition: The place someone is travelling to; it shares destinare but names a place, not a fate.
entries.definitionCN: 旅行的目的地；共享 destinare，但指地点而非命运。

entries.definition: Certain to do or become something.
To intend or set apart for a purpose.
What is going to happen, especially something bad.
entries.definitionCN: 将要发生的事，尤指不好的。

entries.definition: Chance or luck, especially as it affects a life.
entries.definitionCN: 机遇或运气，尤指影响人生的。

entries.definition: A terrible fate that cannot be avoided.

normalIntro.en: Destiny is destin- appoint: what has already been set down for you, like a switch fixed on a track.
normalIntro.cn: destiny 就是 destin-（指定）：早已为你定好的东西，像铁轨上扳好的道岔。

normal.en: Destin- means appointed, as in destination.
normal.cn: destin- 意为指定好的，如 destination。

normal.en: Destiny is the noun, destined the adjective.
normal.cn: destiny 是名词，destined 是形容词。

normal.en: Control your destiny means decide it yourself.
normal.cn: control your destiny 就是自己决定。

normal.en: Fate is often bad, destiny can be great.
normal.cn: fate 常指坏事，destiny 可以是伟大的。

normal.en: A sense of destiny is a feeling of calling.
normal.cn: a sense of destiny 是一种使命感。

abstract.en: A single rail running forward into fog.

examples.cn: 他塑造了自己的命运。

examples.en: Their destinies were linked by the war.
examples.cn: 战争把他们的命运连在一起。

examples.en: She felt destiny calling her to the sea.
examples.cn: 她感到命运在召唤她出海。

sensesIntro.en: One fixed track: a rail in fog, a set switch and a sealed map.
sensesIntro.cn: 同一条定好的轨道：雾中的铁轨、扳好的道岔与一张密封地图。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a single rail running forward into fog with the junction switch already set

branches.en: A single rail running forward into fog.
branches.cn: 一条在雾中向前延伸的铁轨。

branches.en: A switch already set on a track junction.
branches.cn: 道岔口一个早已扳好的开关。

branches.en: A young officer handed a sealed map.

branches.en: Both treat the outcome as already fixed.

branches.en: Both point to a purpose beyond the person.

intro.en: Destiny is destin- plus -y; the appoint root also builds destination and destined.

latinIntro.en: Latin stare means to stand, destinare to make firm and fatum what has been spoken.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 stare 意为站立，destinare 意为使确定，fatum 意为已被说出的事。

definition_zh: 摧毁；毁掉；消灭
definition_en: to damage something so badly that it no longer exists or works
core_image: 一堵墙被推倒，砖块和灰一起落到地上
scene: 拆迁队把最后一面墙推倒，灰尘慢慢散开。The fire destroyed the whole warehouse in an hour.
sceneCN: 这里 destroy 指「摧毁」（第 1 个义项：彻底破坏到无法再用）；句意是那场火在一个小时内烧毁了整座仓库。

senses.title: Break it beyond repair
senses.definition: to damage something so badly that nothing useful is left
senses.definitionCN: 破坏得极其严重，不剩下任何有用的部分
senses.example: The fire destroyed the whole warehouse in an hour.
senses.exampleCN: 那场火在一个小时内烧毁了整座仓库。
senses.why: Building takes many hands; undoing needs only one force.
senses.whyCN: 建造需要许多双手，拆掉只需一股力气。

senses.title: End something invisible
senses.definition: to end something such as hope, trust or confidence completely
senses.definitionCN: 把希望、信任或信心之类彻底终结
senses.example: One careless word destroyed her confidence.
senses.exampleCN: 一句不慎的话毁掉了她的信心。
senses.why: A word can knock down a wall nobody can see.
senses.whyCN: 一句话就能推倒一堵谁也看不见的墙。

senses.title: Wipe out living things
senses.definition: to kill an animal or defeat an enemy completely
senses.definitionCN: 把动物杀死或把敌人彻底打败
senses.example: The disease destroyed whole herds that winter.
senses.exampleCN: 那年冬天，这种病消灭了整群整群的牲畜。
senses.why: The same force that breaks stone can empty a field of animals.
senses.whyCN: 打碎石头的力气，也能让一片田野不再有牲畜。

intro.en: Destroy comes from Latin destruere, to unbuild, built on de-, down, and struere, to pile up or build.
intro.cn: destroy 来自拉丁语 destruere（拆掉建筑），由 de-（向下）与 struere（堆起、建造）构成。

items.en: Struere meant to pile up stones, and de- reversed the piling.
items.cn: struere 指把石头堆起来，前缀 de- 把这堆叠反过来。

items.en: Destruere was used for pulling down walls and for ruining plans.
items.cn: destruere 既用于拆墙，也用于毁掉计划。

items.en: Destruire carried both the physical and the moral sense.
items.cn: destruire 同时带着物质与道义两层意思。

items.en: English destroy covered buildings, armies and reputations.
items.cn: 英语的 destroy 涵盖建筑、军队与名声。

items.en: Today it also names what pollution and fire do to the natural world.
items.cn: 如今它也指污染与大火对自然所做的事。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the same stem, and the meaning group all leave something in pieces.
note.cn: 形近组共用同一词干，近义组则都把某物弄得支离破碎。

entries.definition: a person or ship that destroys
causing great damage
the act or result of destroying
to spoil something completely
to pull a building down
to damage something badly by force

normalIntro.en: These hooks begin with a falling wall and end with an empty field where animals used to stand.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从一堵倒下的墙开始，落到一片曾经站着牲畜的空地。

normal.en: De- plus struere is un-building: the pile is taken apart.
normal.cn: de- 加 struere 就是拆建：把那堆东西拆开。

normal.en: A builder needs a year; a fire needs an hour.
normal.cn: 建造者要一年，一场火只要一个小时。

normal.en: Words destroy confidence with the same ease as fire destroys wood.
normal.cn: 言语毁掉信心，就像火烧掉木头一样容易。

normal.en: The word can empty a building, a hope or a field.
normal.cn: 这个词能让一栋房子、一份希望或一片田野空掉。

normal.en: Add in- and the wall refuses to fall.
normal.cn: 加上 in-，那堵墙就不肯倒了。

abstract.en: Picture bricks sliding out of a wall one course at a time.
abstract.cn: 想象砖块一层层从墙上滑落。

abstract.en: Picture a letter torn once and then again.
abstract.cn: 想象一封信被撕了一次，又被撕了一次。

abstract.en: Picture a fire glowing behind a warehouse window.
abstract.cn: 想象仓库窗后透出一片火光。

examples.en: The fire destroyed the whole warehouse in an hour.
examples.cn: 那场火在一个小时内烧毁了整座仓库。

examples.en: One careless word destroyed her confidence.
examples.cn: 一句不慎的话毁掉了她的信心。

examples.en: The disease destroyed whole herds that winter.
examples.cn: 那年冬天，这种病消灭了整群整群的牲畜。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 destroy 记成「地死拖伊」：de 是去掉，stroy 像「堆」，把堆好的东西拖散，就是摧毁。

root: 来自拉丁语 destruere，由 de-（向下、去掉）与 struere（堆起、建造）组成，经古法语 destruire 进入英语。本义是把堆好的建筑拆掉，后来扩展到毁掉希望与名声，也指消灭大批动物或彻底打败敌人。

sensesIntro.en: From a wall taken apart stone by stone, to a confidence broken by a word, to a herd wiped out.
sensesIntro.cn: 从一块块拆掉的墙，到被一句话击碎的信心，再到整群被消灭的牲畜。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a built thing coming apart faster than it was built.
core.cn: 核心意象：建起来的东西散得比建时更快。

branches.en: The first sense is the physical pile coming down.
branches.cn: 第一个义项是那堆实物塌下来。

branches.en: The second sense is an invisible wall coming down.
branches.cn: 第二个义项是一堵看不见的墙塌下来。

branches.en: The third sense is a living population erased.
branches.cn: 第三个义项是一群活物被抹去。

branches.en: Bricks and confidence both fall when their supports are removed.
branches.cn: 砖块与信心，在支撑被抽走时都会倒下。

branches.en: Fire, flood and disease all use the same verb.
branches.cn: 火、洪水与疾病，用的都是同一个动词。

intro.en: Destroy gives a large family about pulling down, from the person who does it to the thing that cannot be undone.
intro.cn: destroy 给出一大族表示拆毁的词，从动手的人到无法被拆掉的东西。

latinIntro.en: The base is Latin struere, to build, and de- turns building into un-building.
latinIntro.cn: 它的词基是拉丁语 struere（建造），前缀 de- 把建造变成拆毁。

items.exampleCN: 高温会破坏这种维生素。

items.example: The town was destroyed in a night.
items.exampleCN: 这座镇子一夜之间被毁。

items.example: They are destroying the old wall.

items.meaning: one who destroys, or a warship
items.exampleCN: 那艘驱逐舰离开了港口。
这场风暴造成了巨大破坏。
这个箱子好像怎么都弄不坏。

definition_zh: 破坏；毁灭；摧毁
definition_en: the act of destroying something, or the state of being destroyed
core_image: 大风过后，屋顶只剩几根横梁对着天
scene: 洪水退去后，街上堆着断掉的木梁和碎瓦。The storm left a wide trail of destruction.
sceneCN: 这里 destruction 指「破坏」（第 1 个义项：被彻底毁坏的状态与痕迹）；句意是这场风暴留下了一大片破坏的痕迹。

senses.title: The state of being wrecked
senses.definition: the state of having been badly damaged or completely ruined
senses.definitionCN: 已被严重损坏或彻底毁掉的状态
senses.example: The storm left a wide trail of destruction.
senses.exampleCN: 这场风暴留下了一大片破坏的痕迹。
senses.why: After the force passes, the damage stays behind as a landscape.
senses.whyCN: 那股力量过去之后，损坏留在原地，成了一道风景。

senses.title: The act of tearing down
senses.definition: the deliberate act of destroying a building or an object
senses.definitionCN: 有意把建筑或物体毁掉的行为
senses.example: The destruction of the old bridge took two days.
senses.exampleCN: 拆除那座旧桥花了两天。
senses.why: Someone has to decide, bring tools and begin.
senses.whyCN: 总得有人下决定、带工具，然后动手。

senses.title: The thing that ruins you
senses.definition: a person or quality that causes someone's downfall
senses.definitionCN: 导致某人走向败亡的人或品质
senses.example: In the end, his own pride was his destruction.
senses.exampleCN: 最终，他自己的骄傲成了他的祸根。
senses.why: What destroys a person can be carried inside him all along.
senses.whyCN: 毁掉一个人的东西，可能一直就装在他自己身上。

intro.en: Destruction is Latin destructio, from destruere, to unbuild, built on de- and struere, to pile up.
intro.cn: destruction 是拉丁语 destructio，源于 destruere（拆建），由 de- 与 struere（堆起）构成。

items.en: Destructio named the pulling down of a structure.
items.cn: destructio 指把一座建筑拉倒。

items.en: It also covered the ruin of a city, a plan or a life.
items.cn: 它同样涵盖城市、计划或人生的毁败。

items.en: French destruccion kept the double weight of act and result.
items.cn: 法语 destruccion 保留了行为与结果的双重分量。

items.en: English used it for wars, fires and moral ruin alike.
items.cn: 英语把它同样用于战争、火灾与道德上的败亡。

items.en: Modern usage adds the slow destruction of forests and climate.
items.cn: 现代用法又添上了森林与气候那种缓慢的破坏。

note.en: The look-alike group all end in -struction or -struction-like shapes, and the meaning group all name serious damage.
note.cn: 形近组都以 -struction 一类的形状收尾，近义组则都指严重的损坏。

entries.definition: the work of building something
information telling you how to do something
entries.definitionCN: 说明如何做某事的信息

entries.definition: something that blocks the way
the state of being spoiled or lost
great damage over a wide area
entries.definitionCN: 大范围内的大规模损害

entries.definition: harm done to something

normalIntro.en: These hooks begin with a roof open to the sky and end with a man undone by his own pride.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从一顶对着天空敞开的屋顶开始，落到一个被自己骄傲毁掉的人。

normal.en: Construction and destruction differ by one small prefix.
normal.cn: 建造与毁坏，只差一个小前缀。

normal.en: The noun keeps what the verb has already finished.
normal.cn: 动词做完的事，名词把它留在原地。

normal.en: A storm leaves destruction; a decision leaves it too.
normal.cn: 风暴留下破坏，一个决定同样会留下破坏。

normal.en: The word can describe a city, a forest or a single life.
normal.cn: 这个词能形容一座城、一片林，也能形容一个人的一生。

normal.en: What ruins a man may be the very thing he is proud of.
normal.cn: 毁掉一个人的，也许正是他最引以为傲的东西。

abstract.en: Picture a roof frame with nothing left above it.
abstract.cn: 想象一副屋顶的骨架，上面什么都没有了。

abstract.en: Picture a street covered in wet broken tiles.
abstract.cn: 想象一条街铺满湿透的碎瓦。

abstract.en: Picture a mirror cracked across the middle.
abstract.cn: 想象一面从中间裂开的镜子。

examples.en: The storm left a wide trail of destruction.
examples.cn: 这场风暴留下了一大片破坏的痕迹。

examples.en: The destruction of the old bridge took two days.
examples.cn: 拆除那座旧桥花了两天。

examples.en: In the end, his own pride was his destruction.
examples.cn: 最终，他自己的骄傲成了他的祸根。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 destruction 记成「地斯抓克神」：de 是去掉，struct 是建造，建造被去掉，就成了破坏。

root: 来自拉丁语 destructio，源于 destruere（拆掉建筑），由 de-（去掉）与 struere（堆起、建造）构成。本义是建筑被拉倒，后来指城市、计划与人生的毁败，现代又指森林与气候那种缓慢而大范围的破坏。

sensesIntro.en: From the wreck left after a force passes, to the deliberate tearing down, to the flaw inside a person.
sensesIntro.cn: 从力量过后留下的残骸，到有意的拆除，再到一个人心里的那处缺口。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a structure standing open to the sky.
core.cn: 核心意象：一座向天空敞开的建筑残骸。

branches.en: The first sense is the wreck as it lies there afterward.
branches.cn: 第一个义项是事后躺在那里的残骸。

branches.en: The second sense is the work of pulling it down.
branches.cn: 第二个义项是把它拉倒的那份劳作。

branches.en: The third sense is a ruin that comes from inside.
branches.cn: 第三个义项是从内部生出的毁败。

branches.en: A noun can hold both the deed and the debris.
branches.cn: 一个名词可以同时装着行为与废堆。

branches.en: Storms ruin towns, and pride ruins the man who owns it.
branches.cn: 风暴毁掉城镇，骄傲毁掉拥有它的人。

intro.en: Destruction grows words for the quality, the manner and the impossibility of being destroyed.
intro.cn: destruction 长出表示性质、方式以及「无法被毁」的一族词。

latinIntro.en: The base is Latin struere, to build, and de- turns the building around; -tion makes the act a noun.
latinIntro.cn: 它的词基是拉丁语 struere（建造），de- 把建造掉转方向，-tion 把动作变成名词。

items.meaning: the act or result of destroying
items.exampleCN: 这场风暴造成了巨大破坏。
这些甲虫破坏性地蔓延。
他们测量了这场风暴的破坏力。

items.meaning: one who destroys, or a warship
items.exampleCN: 那艘驱逐舰离开了港口。

items.example: The town was destroyed in a night.
items.exampleCN: 这座镇子一夜之间被毁。
这个箱子好像怎么都弄不坏。

definition_zh: adj. 破坏的；破坏性的；毁灭的；（对己）自毁的
definition_en: causing great damage to things, people or relationships, or likely to harm the person doing it
core_image: 一面墙被推倒，砖块散在脚下；一段关系里，每次开口都留下裂痕
scene: 批评可以是破坏性的。Criticism can be destructive.
sceneCN: 第 1 个义项：destructive 指破坏性的；句意是批评可以是破坏性的。

pos.zh: 破坏的；破坏性的；毁灭的

senses.title: Causing physical damage
senses.definition: causing great damage to things or places
senses.definitionCN: 对物品或地方造成严重损坏
senses.example: The storm was destructive along the coast.
senses.exampleCN: 这场风暴在沿海一带破坏力极大。
senses.why: A wall pushed over with bricks at your feet.
senses.whyCN: 一面被推倒的墙，砖块散在脚下。

senses.title: Harming people or feelings
senses.definition: causing harm to a person, a relationship or confidence
senses.definitionCN: 对人、关系或信心造成伤害
senses.example: Destructive criticism leaves nothing to build on.
senses.exampleCN: 破坏性批评让人无从改进。
senses.why: A crack widening in a shared wall.
senses.whyCN: 共用墙上一道不断变宽的裂缝。

senses.title: Tending to harm oneself
senses.definition: likely to harm the person or thing doing it
senses.definitionCN: 可能伤害行为者自身的
senses.example: The habit became self-destructive.
senses.exampleCN: 这个习惯变成了自我毁灭。
senses.why: A fire burning its own fuel supply.
senses.whyCN: 一场烧掉自身燃料的火。

intro.en: Destructive comes from Latin destructivus, from destruere, de- down plus struere to build, so literally to unbuild what was built.
intro.cn: destructive 源自拉丁语 destructivus，来自 destruere，由 de-（向下）加 struere（建造）构成，字面就是「拆掉建好的东西」。

items.en: Struere meant to build or pile up.
items.cn: struere 意为建造、堆起。

items.en: Destruere meant to pull down what was built.
items.cn: destruere 意为拆掉建好的东西。

items.en: Destructivus meant tending to pull down.
items.cn: destructivus 意为倾向于拆毁的。

items.en: Destructive entered English for causing ruin.
items.cn: 十五世纪 destructive 以造成毁坏义进入英语。

items.en: It widened to harm to feelings and habits.
items.cn: 十九世纪扩展到对感情与习惯的伤害。

items.en: Self-destructive now describes harmful behaviour.
items.cn: 如今 self-destructive 用来描述自毁行为。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the struct- build family; the near-meaning group names other ways of causing harm.
note.cn: 形近组共享 struct-（建造）家族；近义组是其他表示「造成伤害」的词。

entries.definition: The act of building; it shares struere but puts things up instead of pulling them down.
entries.definitionCN: 建造的行为；共享 struere，但是立起来而非拆下去。

entries.definition: Teaching or an order; it shares the struct- stem but concerns knowledge.
entries.definitionCN: 教学或指令；共享 struct- 词干，但关乎知识。

entries.definition: The act of destroying something.
Having a bad effect on something.
Likely to cause damage or injury.
Causing very great damage or shock.

normalIntro.en: Destructive is de- down plus struct- build plus -ive tending to: tending to pull down what was built.
normalIntro.cn: destructive 就是 de-（向下）加 struct-（建造）加 -ive（倾向于）：倾向于把建好的东西拆下来。

normal.en: Struct- means build, as in structure.
normal.cn: struct- 意为建造，如 structure。

normal.en: De- turns building into unbuilding.
normal.cn: de- 把建造变成拆毁。

normal.en: -ive means tending to.
normal.cn: -ive 表示倾向于。

normal.en: Destructive criticism only tears down.
normal.cn: destructive criticism 只会拆台。

normal.en: Self-destructive harms the doer.
normal.cn: self-destructive 伤害的是行为者自己。

abstract.en: A wall pushed over with bricks at your feet.
abstract.cn: 一面被推倒的墙，砖块散在脚下。

abstract.en: A crack widening in a shared wall.
